## SECTION 6: EU processes

_Slug: eu_processes_

_Layout: Slide with mininal content_

_Source: 1-AFFILIATE_i1.pptx | pptx | Slide 6_

_Signals: medium (words=87, tables=0)_

- When following the EU CP process, LMG will initiate the BLUE project following EMA submission, instead of the RA Representative.
- For EU type II variations, artwork start date is within 14 calendar days from CHMP Opinion/Reference Member State approval
- The Affiliate uploads briefing documents in BLUE within 14 calendar days from CHMP opinion/RMS approval

- 6

- LMG initiates the BLUE project for EU Centralised Procedure projects.

- For all other EU submission types (e.g., MRP/DCP, NP) the BLUE project must be initiated within 14 calendar days from CHMP/RMS approval

## SECTION 19: POC Takeaways â€“ As of Aug 2022

_Slug: poc_takeaways_as_of_aug_2022_

_Layout: Slide with mininal content_

_Source: 1-AFFILIATE_i1.pptx | pptx | Slide 19_

_Signals: medium (words=119, tables=1)_

- Initial Impressions
- L2P has received positive feedback from individuals involved in the BLUE project initiation process in Canada, Germany, Mexico, Thailand, & Vietnam.
- Specific feedback includes (paraphrased):
- The Expedited Implementation Process is a welcome change which will help reduce implementation times (Germany, Thailand, Vietnam)
- The additional development cycle is negligible compared to the gain in the implementation time (Canada, Mexico)
- Colombia
- The Colombian HA was subject of a Ransomware attack which significantly affected the ability of the HA to conduct routine business.  Submission of the RSP and HA feedback was delayed.
- Although the unavoidable hurdle was encountered, the BLUE project was able to be initiated and artwork development got underway in alignment with the Expedited Implementation Process timeline.

## SECTION 30: inspection findings

_Slug: inspection_findings_

_Layout: Slide with heavy content_

_Source: 1-AFFILIATE_i1.pptx | pptx | Slide 30_

_Signals: medium (words=114, tables=0)_

- BfArM & MHRA requirements:
- Decision was made in December 2020 to bring the BfArM preventive action under the L2P project
- Performed a root cause analysis and reviewed if planned L2P deliverables were sufficient (slide 4-5)
- Identified the need to improve communication and decided to set-up a new committee responsible for planning and oversight of safety changes to labels up until implementation
- The team committed to updating any relevant QDs, if needed, before December 2021
- More information:
- BfArM inspection findings, responses and Preventive Actions
- Letter from Regional Government of Upper Bavaria (22 feb2021)
- Summary of MHRA inspection findings (shared by PV on 1st March 2021)
- High level summary of inspection findings on the next slide

---

## SECTION 31: High level Summary of findings (details in back-up slides)

_Slug: high_level_summary_of_findings_details_in_back_up_slides_

_Layout: Slide with heavy content_

_Source: 1-AFFILIATE_i1.pptx | pptx | Slide 31_

_Signals: medium (words=179, tables=0)_

- BfArM inspection findings:
- The implementation of the variations for the artwork, in particular the package leaflet, may take place within a period of 5.25 months (regulatory procedure approval up to artwork approval 42 days and a further 105 days from artwork approval).
- However, once the change in artwork has been approved by the regulatory authority, it is no longer considered approval-compliant manufacturing or contract manufacturing, as a non-approval compliant package leaflet is released and used in secondary packaging.
- This excessively long period of 5.25 months has not been assessed as part of quality risk management
- Regional Government of Upper Bavaria:
- According to BfArM, safety related variations are to be implemented at the next production run/next printing.
- Meaning of â€œimplementationâ€ is when the company internally approves the revised product information. The revised product information should normally be used in the next packaging run.
- MHRA:
- After MHRA approval, changes to labels with updated safety information, leaflets and packages must be introduced within 3-6 months
- The MAH should update the EMC (Electronic Medicines Compendium) website within 10 working days after regulatory approval

- The new L2P process did in fact yield an efficiency gain in the timeline from â€œHA Approvalâ€ to â€œAffiliate Approvalâ€ (as expected), however opportunities exist to further expedite the implementation process.
- Further efficiency gains may be achieved by:

## SECTION 13: Artwork Development Cycle Analysis Results

_Slug: artwork_development_cycle_analysis_results_

_Layout: Slide with mininal content_

_Source: PoC Data Analysis.pptx | pptx | Slide 13_

_Signals: high (words=108, tables=2)_

- The Artwork Development Cycle findings from the PoC show an increase of 1.33 cycles on average
- Upon further investigation, the team identified that Canada (which has a unique process) is driving the increase
- Excluding Canada from the dataset yields an increase of 1.02 cycles per project which is in alignment with projections

- 13

- We include Canada in the dataset by dividing the number or artwork cycles for Canada by 2, as 2 artworks are required in Canada, thus yielding an increase of 0.97 cycles per project
- In Canada, both English and French artwork is required.  Therefore, the number of artwork development cycles required is double that other countries.

## SECTION 16: Results

_Slug: results_

_Layout: Slide with mininal content_

_Source: PoC Data Analysis.pptx | pptx | Slide 16_

_Signals: medium (words=143, tables=0)_

- The analysis of the data from the PoC shows the following results by success parameter:
- Process Efficiency
- A 26-day gain in process efficiency from HA Approval ïƒ  BOM Update
- Implementation Timeline
- 3-month Implementation is feasible based on Affiliate Approval being reached 49 days, leaving 41 days for BOM Implementation
- Note:  As agreed within the L2P project team, the 3-month timeline for implementation from HA Approval is a goal for the process, but is not defined in our QDs as a process requirement
- Number of Artwork Cycles
- The number of artwork cycles is consistent with projections at an increase of 0.97 cycles per project
- Cost/Resources for AWM
- Resource implications for LMG are consistent with original projection of 0.3 FTE
- Cost/Resources for RA Affiliates
- No resource implications on RA Affiliates
- Cost/Resources for RA CCDS & Labeling
- No resource implications on RA CCDS & Labeling

| SOP-2290 | Artwork Approval Process and Artwork Text Management for New or Revised Printed Packaging Component | Technology & Manufacturing (T&M)/SCM | For important safety variations, start a BLUE Project within 14 calendar days after RSP submission. / For EU type II variation, RA Representative will upload briefing document in BLUE within 14 calendar days from CHMP opinion/Reference Member State approval. / LMG starts BLUE project for Centralized Procedure / Additionally for SOP-2293: For Important Safety Variations for EU CP to EMA, ASD is 14 calendars days after submission of the centralized RSP to EMA. |
| SOP-2293 | Artwork Development with AMS BLUE | T&M/SCM | For important safety variations, start a BLUE Project within 14 calendar days after Regulatory Submission Package (RSP) submission. / For EU type II variation, RA Representative will upload briefing document in BLUE within 14 calendar days from CHMP opinion/Reference Member State approval. / LMG will start the BLUE project for Centralized Procedure |
| STL-4270 | Ultimate Implementation Date (Definitions and Timelines) | T&M/SCM | Reference to importance safety variations for regulatory procedure driven changes for EMEA and Asian Region (Leaflet). |

## SECTION 5: L2P Scope & Benefits

_Slug: l2p_scope_benefits_

_Layout: Slide with heavy content_

_Source: L2P Introduction - Oct 2022.pptx | pptx | Slide 5_

_Signals: medium (words=105, tables=0)_

- Project Scope
- Develop a globally harmonized and efficient end-to-end process from HA approval of the updated Label until distribution of the updated Package, including clearly defined roles, responsibilities, and handovers
- Define end-to-end KPIs/metrics (from Safety Signal ïƒ  Distribution) to plan critical steps and monitor progress (i.e., planning, oversight, and performance)
- Develop dashboards/reports that extract KPIs/metrics from relevant source systems
- Project Benefits
- A harmonized global process, improved oversight, accurate planning and tracking, clear roles and responsibilities, and efficient handovers will support timely implementation of the updated Package
- All of the above is expected to improve the efficiency of the RA, Artwork Management, and Supply Chain organizations

## SECTION 10: POC Takeaways â€“ As of Aug 2022

_Signals: medium (words=119, tables=1)_

- Initial Impressions
- L2P has received positive feedback from individuals involved in the BLUE project initiation process in Canada, Germany, Mexico, Thailand, & Vietnam.
- Specific feedback includes (paraphrased):
- The Expedited Implementation Process is a welcome change which will help reduce implementation times (Germany, Thailand, Vietnam)
- The additional development cycle is negligible compared to the gain in the implementation time (Canada, Mexico)
- Colombia
- The Colombian HA was subject of a Ransomware attack which significantly affected the ability of the HA to conduct routine business.  Submission of the RSP and HA feedback was delayed.
- Although the unavoidable hurdle was encountered, the BLUE project was able to be initiated and artwork development got underway in alignment with the Expedited Implementation Process timeline.

## SECTION 24: inspection findings

_Slug: inspection_findings_

_Layout: Slide with heavy content_

_Source: L2P Introduction - Oct 2022.pptx | pptx | Slide 24_

_Signals: medium (words=114, tables=0)_

- BfArM & MHRA requirements:
- Decision was made in December 2020 to bring the BfArM preventive action under the L2P project
- Performed a root cause analysis and reviewed if planned L2P deliverables were sufficient (slide 4-5)
- Identified the need to improve communication and decided to set-up a new committee responsible for planning and oversight of safety changes to labels up until implementation
- The team committed to updating any relevant QDs, if needed, before December 2021
- More information:
- BfArM inspection findings, responses and Preventive Actions
- Letter from Regional Government of Upper Bavaria (22 feb2021)
- Summary of MHRA inspection findings (shared by PV on 1st March 2021)
- High level summary of inspection findings on the next slide

---

## SECTION 25: High level Summary of findings (details in back-up slides)

_Slug: high_level_summary_of_findings_details_in_back_up_slides_

_Layout: Slide with heavy content_

_Source: L2P Introduction - Oct 2022.pptx | pptx | Slide 25_

_Signals: medium (words=179, tables=0)_

- BfArM inspection findings:
- The implementation of the variations for the artwork, in particular the package leaflet, may take place within a period of 5.25 months (regulatory procedure approval up to artwork approval 42 days and a further 105 days from artwork approval).
- However, once the change in artwork has been approved by the regulatory authority, it is no longer considered approval-compliant manufacturing or contract manufacturing, as a non-approval compliant package leaflet is released and used in secondary packaging.
- This excessively long period of 5.25 months has not been assessed as part of quality risk management
- Regional Government of Upper Bavaria:
- According to BfArM, safety related variations are to be implemented at the next production run/next printing.
- Meaning of â€œimplementationâ€ is when the company internally approves the revised product information. The revised product information should normally be used in the next packaging run.
- MHRA:
- After MHRA approval, changes to labels with updated safety information, leaflets and packages must be introduced within 3-6 months
- The MAH should update the EMC (Electronic Medicines Compendium) website within 10 working days after regulatory approval

## SECTION 9: the scope for the PoC

_Layout: Slide with heavy content_

- Propose to execute the PoC with the next important safety change
- Select approximately 10 countries that follow the new process (PoC countries)
- The other countries follow the current process (non-PoC countries)
- PoC country selection criteria:
- Countries from at least 2 regions
- A change manufactured by Kerry or Meppel
- A change manufactured by a CMO
- Compare parameters from PoC countries with non-PoC countries with the same safety change (internal comparison) and to historical data

## SECTION 16: Decision to start PoC

_Slug: decision_to_start_poc_

_Layout: Slide with heavy content_

_Source: L2P SC meeting - 20220210 - final.pptx | pptx | Slide 16_

_Signals: medium (words=165, tables=0)_

- Summary of the proposal:
- The team has designed the PoC study, including parameters to be measured
- The proposal is to conduct the PoC with the next important safety change, i.e. Tacrolimus
- The country selection is ongoing, but the intent is to select 10 Tier 1 countries and a 3-5 Tier 2 countries to conduct the new process (create the BLUE project 14 days after HA submission)
- The other countries in which the Tacrolimus change is submitted will follow the current process (create the BLUE project 7 days after HA approval)
- Data collection will take place until December 2022 (1st analysis) for Tier 1 countries
- Based on that data set, theÂ team will advise the L2P SC on next decisions:
- Implement the new process (most PoC parameters are green)
- Do not implement the new process (most PoC are red)
- Wait until the Tier 2 data is collected to take a decision
- Decision required: Does the SC agree to conduct the PoC study as outlined above?

- 16

- Bill - Well good evening Product Safety fans. I am Bill Billison and we are once again, now, mere moments away from another chapter in what has now become an ongoing saga across the pharma and biopharma industry: the Cross-Functional Signal to Label to Package Obstacle Course Relay Race (CFSLPOCRR) as itâ€™s known around these studios.
- Bill - It wasn't long ago we thought we knew everything there was to know about updating labels from a safety signal.
- Bill - But now this scrappy upstart within Astellas â€“ conventionally called Team Blue or the L2P Transformation Team â€“ have taken the Process World by storm with what can only be described as a rise as meteoric as it was ambitious.
- Bill - Jane Janeson is standing by trackside as the Teams configure their courses.
- Bill - Jane, the experts will probably disagree but it really seems like we havenâ€™t seen something like this before: an unknown team, tasked with a difficult but predictable change management, who manages to somehow, come out of nowhere to entirely revolutionize the sport. Is that just me?
- Jane - Youâ€™re right, Bill. You know if you talk to this Label to Pack Team, theyâ€™re just doing their job.  Theyâ€™ll tell you they learned from other Affiliates that had configured their courses similarly. And while thatâ€™s certainly true, they are certainly standing on the shoulders of giants, itâ€™s hard to feel like thereâ€™s also something fundamentally different about this contest today. Thereâ€™s an energy trackside that I havenâ€™t felt in my many years of being involved with Package Change activities.
- Bill - Take us through it Jane.  Weâ€™ve seen such great things from the Astellas and Affiliate Squads through the years. Why the excitement this time?
- Jane - In essence, Bill: Process and Automation. Iâ€™m told the L2P Team has made changes not just to the design of their course â€“ their Process â€“ but also to how they communicate  cross-functionally  through something theyâ€™re calling the AIC Dashboard.
- Bill - That was something that originally met with some skepticism, right. Something as complex and cross-functional as Label and Package changes have not leant themselves to simple or easy automation.
- Jane - I think if you talk with the Team, theyâ€™ll tell you thereâ€™s not much simple about it. But youâ€™re right: a couple years ago, I wouldâ€™ve said it was impossible. But theyâ€™ve got the Dashboard feeding them data from Safety Evaluation Approval Date all the way through Market Release Date. They will be able to use this information IN REAL TIME during the Race, Bill, increasing their response time, improving visibility with their stakeholders, and virtually eliminating all the cumbersome back and forth that you and I have come to accept as just a reality of the Signal to Package Relay Race.
- Bill - Thatâ€™s amazing.
- Jane - It really is. That dashboard, along with their process changes, this will really be something to watch.
- Bill - Thanks Jane.
- Bill - Well, the game has certainly changed but the race has largely stayed the same. Joining me now, Doug Douger. Doug?
- Doug - Howdy, Bill
- Bill - Doug, take us through. It what will these teams be looking to accomplish today? How are they gonna do it?
- Doug - Well, theyâ€™re gonna do it by gettin it done fast. As you rightly know, Health Authorities around the world are taking an ever more challenging view of Label and Package Changes not made within a certain period of time. Now thatâ€™s gonna put a lot of pressure on both these teams to not just get through their course, but to get through it right.
- Bill - Break this down for me, Doug. Whatâ€™s really happening? Walk us through it.
- Doug - All right so hereâ€™s L2Pâ€™s gameplan: hereâ€™s your traditional Signal to Label to Package Process map that we just saw live on the course. And the opportunity theyâ€™ve identified is really right here: right at the point of HA submission. You see, youâ€™ve got all this time waiting for the HA response. And what that really means is that process actually looks more like this, with this big wide open space right here waiting for Approval.
- Bill - Well weâ€™re about to find out because itâ€™s race time. Jane, whatâ€™s happening down there?
- Jane - Excitement, Bill. It started off as you might expect, with these two teams going about their normal process. But even there, Team Blue has been a little quicker throughout because of their dashboard communications. And now you can see weâ€™re getting to the real moment. Team Blue is just about to, yes, there they go! Team Blue is moving onto Artwork creation!
- Bill - Wow, look at him go! Incredible!
- Doug - Guys, I donâ€™t think this is going to even be close.
- Jane - they both are going to need that HA Approval to move on to reconcile, but already Team Blue has such a lead. Itâ€™s literally just a hop skip and a jump for them now.
- Bill - Jane are we watching history be made?
- Jane - I think so.
- Doug - I think we definitely are!
